data.exact_reserve_text: Of the adverse claims movement of GBP 3.4m in the year ended 31 December 2015, GBP 0.4m related to the older years 2006-2010 which appear to have achieved a degree of stability, GBP 2.2m to the 2011 year of account and GBP 0.8m to the pure year of account.

named_events.loss_description: significant property losses which have stemmed from a number of CAT events in Australia and the UK, the largest of which was Storm Desmond in December 2015. The two main CAT events have given rise to a gross loss of GBP 4.8m and net loss of GBP 1.8m.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross prior year reserve strengthening of GBP 3.4 million, primarily due to adverse claims development across older years of account, specifically GBP 0.4 million for 2006-2010, GBP 2.2 million for 2011, and GBP 0.8 million for the 2012 year of account. This movement occurred amidst ongoing uncertainty regarding final losses, potential tax rebates not yet recognized, and reserving volatility, which also led to the 2012 and 2013 years of account being placed into run-off.
raw_causal_phrases: adverse movement experienced in older years of account
on-going uncertainty over the final loss arising from a combination of factors
potential tax rebate of GBP 2.8m, not held on the balance sheet
continuing assessment of the reserving position due to volatility experienced
similar uncertainty existing on a potential tax rebate of up to GBP 1.0m and with reserving uncertainties to also consider

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property
